domain_description: Teaching students whose home language is not the language of instruction — the design moves that keep cognitive demand high while making the language accessible. Vocabulary tiering, sentence frames, language-demand analysis, sheltered-instruction protocols, and scaffolded task modification. Built on the Cummins BICS/CALP distinction, Echevarria/Vogt/Short's SIOP model, and Beck/McKeown/Kucan's tiered vocabulary work, with meta-analytic evidence from Cheung & Slavin, Goldenberg, and the broader EAL/ELL research tradition.

skills.description: Generate tiered sentence frames that let EAL students participate in academic discourse before they have fully independent academic language. Frames are scaffolds, not scripts: they expose the syntax and discourse markers of a subject, then fade as students take them over.
skills.effect_months_source: EEF Toolkit — Oral language interventions strand
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Frames are paper or screen — no materials cost. The lift is teacher design time: building frames that match the discourse of the subject, tiering them across proficiency levels, and remembering to fade them as students internalise the patterns. EEF Oral language interventions strand carries +6 months on high-security evidence (154 studies); sentence frames are one well-established scaffold within that strand but have no clean standalone meta-analysis. The 2023 "over-framing" critique (Lemov et al.) is worth heeding — frames that are never faded become language restrictions rather than supports.
